findings.finding: What the price already assumes reverses once the 10-Q debt is in. The red-team audit (fundamental_engine.redteam.audit) on the capital structure as run (debt $12.579B) FAILS the critical check debt_complete against the 10-Q principal of $125.337B. With the 10-Q debt it passes. I reran expectation_gap (fundamental_engine.expectations) as a reviewer cross-check. It is a simplified driver model with my own anchors: revenue0 = FY2027 guide $90B, g1 44.4% (base growth_anchor) for 3 years fading to 4.2%, margin 30%, tax 15%, sales_to_capital 0.5, terminal ROIC 13%, rate 10.69% (model cost of equity), cash $37.08B, shares 3,055M including the converted preferred. Results at the run's debt: value $172, and the price needs only 36% growth, 1 high-growth year, a 27.7% margin or sales_to_capital 0.44. Results at the 10-Q debt: value $135 vs the $141.80 quote, and the price needs 46% growth, 4 high-growth years, a 30.5% margin (the best 3-year margin is 30.8%) or sales_to_capital 0.51. That is a little MORE than management's full plan. The implied 5-year revenue CAGR of about 41% compares with a demonstrated 3-year CAGR of 10.5%. The +45% 'discount to base' in the run is an artifact of the missing debt. Correctly read, the price already pays for the FY2028-FY2030 targets delivered on time, with no cushion. P(beat) is unassessed (no base-rate function supplied).

findings.finding: There is an engine anomaly in the financing and terminal logic. In the scratchpad diagnostic, adding $118B of debt RAISED the base value (206 to 214) and the bull value (459 to 490), while only the bear fell (49 to 36). Equity value cannot rise when debt claims rise and the operating plan is unchanged. Possible causes are a debt-weighted discount rate or terminal WACC that falls with leverage, interest tax shields counted twice, or new draws valued as if they were free cash. Until this is explained, no ORCL scenario value, even a corrected one, can be shown as a conclusion.

findings.fix: Trace the per-share bridge for base at the two opening debts (EV, the discount rate used each year and in the terminal, the debt claim subtracted, draws and their PV) and fix the sign. Add a unit test: more opening debt with the same operating plan must not raise equity value per share. Run the full unittest suite, then rerun ticker-value.

findings.finding: Counter-thesis (pre-mortem, October 2029: ORCL well below $100, the investment failed). (1) Counterparty: about half of the $664B RPO is reportedly one customer, OpenAI (press, unconfirmed by Oracle). That customer could not fund its ramp, and the 10-K itself warns that some OCI customers are highly leveraged. Deliveries were deferred or renegotiated, so OCI revenue lagged the $73B FY2028 target by tens of billions. (2) Duration mismatch: Oracle is locked into $288B of uncommenced 15-19 year data-center leases and $34.6B of lease liabilities, against 1-5 year customer contracts. Lease and depreciation costs arrived on schedule while revenue did not, so operating margin fell well below the 25% bear terminal. (3) Supply response: AWS, Microsoft and Google, which the 10-K names as IaaS rivals, add capacity at 2-4x Oracle's capex, and GPU-hour pricing fell at renewal. (4) Funding spiral: FCF of -$23.7B in FY2026 and -$5.4B in Q1 FY2027 (-$16.8B before $11.4B of prepayments) stayed negative. Debt rose from $125B toward $250B. A downgrade raised the cost of debt, and Oracle issued equity again, as with the $20B ATM in Q1 FY2027 (+5% shares), at lower prices. (5) The legacy cash engine eroded: licenses -15% and support -1% in Q1 FY2027. ROIC fell below the cost of capital (incremental 3.4%). Signals that would have shown it early: RPO stalling or a falling 0-12 month share (12% now); Q2 FY2027 revenue below the $20.9B guide low; capex guidance raised again with the revenue guide only held; a new ATM or equity raise; a rating action or wider spreads; customer prepayments shrinking; Oracle disclosing a customer at 10% or more of revenue; OpenAI financing setbacks; leases commencing faster than OCI revenue grows.

findings.finding: The bear slows growth but does not break the business, and its own events are not sized. Bear revenue still doubles from FY2026's $67.4B to $137.5B in FY2031 (growth_anchor 15%). Bear FY2028 EBIT margin is 30.3% ($31.5B / $103.7B), about the same as base (31.7%). It drifts to 25% only by the late years. Bear growth capex stays at $35-45B a year. The bear events (OpenAI loss, a 15-19 year lease mismatch with costs that 'stay', and a funding gap) imply a revenue shortfall, a fixed-cost deleverage and impairments. None of these is in the bear drivers. The OpenAI effect is the analyst's own '$27B of $73B' arithmetic, not a size taken from its share of RPO (about $300B of $664B per press). The engine itself leaves biz.competition, val.capex_below_history and fin.coverage 'not_priced'.
findings.where: casefile.json val.result.scenarios[0].forecast (revenue, ebit, growth_capex); position.json drivers (bear growth_anchor 0.15, mature_margin 0.25); position/coherence.md bear events 1-4; dc.risk_pricing
findings.fix: Size a bear from the evidence. Take the OCI revenue tied to the press-attributed contract share (labelled hypothesis), deferred or lost from FY2028. Keep lease cost and depreciation on the committed schedule (rp_f_lease_uncommenced_q1fy27), so the margin falls in FY2028-FY2029, not only at maturity. Cut growth capex only as far as commitments allow. Mark biz.competition and val.capex_below_history as priced in that path.

findings.finding: The bear funding story contradicts the bear drivers. A bear event says 'if capital markets close, Oracle issues more shares at a low price', and the key risk cites $125B of debt. But fc.funding.bear has equity_raised 0, new_financing_shares 0 and only $8.4B of debt draws. Bear debt runs $12.6B to $21.0B with interest of about $0.34-0.96B a year, while Oracle reported $1.428B of interest in Q1 FY2027 alone (about $5.7B a year). The bear value of $48.57 therefore omits both the real debt and the dilution its own story describes. In the corrected diagnostic the bear fell to $36.35.

findings.finding: Lease obligations sit outside every scenario. They are $34.6B of recognized lease liabilities and $288B of uncommenced 15-19 year data-center leases (rp_f_lease_uncommenced_q1fy27), more than twice the notes. They are excluded from debt by definition, and the forecast does not show their cost ramp separately. They are the core of the duration-mismatch risk that the key risk itself names. For a capacity seller whose customer contracts run 1-5 years, the lease stream is a fixed claim ahead of equity in the bear.

findings.finding: The base relies on large, uncommitted external financing, yet it is labelled the most likely path. Base debt draws are $31.6B (FY2028), $43.9B (FY2029), $36.0B (FY2030), $24.4B (FY2031) and more in 2032, on top of the missing $113B of opening notes. So real base debt would pass about $260B by FY2031. Interest on that, at the run's 4.6% rate, is roughly $12B a year, against base FY2031 EBIT of $83B. The funding gate already lists assumed_financing_base as unresolved, and nothing tests whether the credit market will fund that path at 4.6%.
findings.fix: After the debt fix, show the base debt and coverage path. Test the interest rate against Oracle's latest issued coupons (10-Q notes table), and add a falsifier on net debt/EBITDA or coverage by FY2028. Keep the 'funding conditional' label visible next to any value.

findings.finding: The bull's conditions have no falsifiers of their own. The bull rests on 'no further equity issues after FY2027' and 'operating margin rising to about 35%', but its two falsifiers are revenue thresholds only. The bear falsifiers (RPO above $700B, Q2 FY2028 revenue above $30B) refute the bear only on growth, not on the margin or funding mechanisms the bear events describe.
